answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a refundable capital bond rather than identity checks. To attest, an operator escrows a fixed stake locked for a full epoch. Creating N sock-puppets costs N times that stake, so a swarm is priced out instead of merely slowed: the attacker must float real value indefinitely, and one slash burns the whole bond. Splitting identities never reduces total locked value. The bond is not a hollow gate; it turns free identity into a walnut-hard commitment, and an attacker who tries a vine of cheap aliases finds every strand equally expensive.
